title: DocGov configuration
description: .docgov/config.yaml — every governance decision is configurable here. A policy pack may set any of these; local config always wins.

mode.description: Decides how much blocks. solo blocks 3 rules; enterprise blocks 12. Over-enforcement is the main reason governance tooling gets uninstalled.

layout.description: compact suits most repositories. full is the numbered 00-canonical…99-archive tree; it earns its overhead at roughly 25+ documents.

exclude.description: Agent infrastructure is excluded by default: governing the files that configure DocGov is not useful.

enforce.description: Rule ids that block. null derives the list from the project mode.

warn_only.description: Nothing blocks. Useful while adopting DocGov on an existing repository.

limits.description: Per document type. Line counts gate whether a semantic review is worth spending; they never trigger an automatic split.

quality.description: Advisory thresholds per type. Never used as a hard gate: a subjective judgement that fails a build is one nobody can appeal.

domains.description: The highest-leverage section. Mapping a domain to code paths is what switches on context packs, invariant injection and drift detection.

policy_packs.description: V3 organizational governance: paths to policy packs whose taxonomy, limits, quality thresholds and invariants layer under this config. The repository always keeps the last word.
